description:
The generators of the dense-parity no-change verdict's drift and assembly records fail on the current tree after a later code change to a file they baseline; a committed record stays verifiable when unrelated work moves on.

## Background

`dev/active/1a379447-zen3-cpu-performance/6e87c436/survey/` holds generators that compare a content-pinned anchor baseline of the two kernel crates with the working tree and write `production-drift.json` and `asm-comparison.json`. They were designed to fail when a baselined file later differs in code. A later fix changed `crates/gf2-core/src/alg/m4rm.rs`, and the generators now stop with "no file holds the baseline digest" instead of reproducing the committed records. The records describe the tree the verdict was issued on; the verdict's claim is about that tree.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A committed check verifies the committed drift and assembly records against content they pin, on any later tree, and exits zero while those pinned contents are present; it writes nothing.
- [hard] REQ-02: Regenerating a record on a tree that differs from the pinned end state refuses to overwrite and says which paths differ, shown by a test on a tree where a baselined file has changed.
- [hard] REQ-03: The verdict's verification document states which tree its records describe and gives the check command; no committed record's bytes change.

## Notes

Found while removing the unselected XOR unroll bodies. Content-anchor tooling shared by later tasks lives under `dev/scripts`.
title: Keep the dense-parity verdict's drift records verifiable on later trees
